column3: The Hebrew says the Spirit was upon Azariah; BSB says came upon him.
The Hebrew names many days without an explicit tense-bearing verb; BSB uses many years and has been.
The Hebrew begins with singular he returned and then switches to plural they sought; BSB uses plural they throughout.
The Hebrew names the one going out and the one coming in and says peace; BSB combines these as travelers and uses safety.
The Hebrew retains slackening hands and says there is a reward for your work; BSB uses discouragement and a passive promise of reward.
The Hebrew names Oded the prophet without Azariah son of; BSB supplies those words. The final portico belongs to the LORD without an explicit word temple.
The Hebrew calls the settlers resident foreigners without explicitly naming tribes; BSB describes people from the tribes who had settled among them.
The Hebrew says that day and has no separate all or back; BSB uses at that time and adds those details.
The Hebrew says from small to great; BSB interprets this as young or old.
The Hebrew says with all their desire; BSB uses earnestly.
The Hebrew calls Maacah the king’s mother and describes her object as a horrifying image made for Asherah; BSB uses grandmother and an Asherah pole.
The Hebrew calls Asa’s heart whole; BSB interprets this as fully devoted.
The Hebrew distinguishes silver, gold, and vessels and repeats dedicated things for father and son; BSB combines them as silver and gold articles.
